_comment: What to read out of Mistral's public pricing page.
It names ROW LABELS, not models. Which models the page shows is Mistral's business
and changes week to week; following that is the whole point of this job. A card
Mistral adds is published on the next run, one it withdraws keeps its last observed
prices and gains an 'absent_since' stamp, and a card it renames is simply a removal
There is no hand-written model list, and there must not be one. An earlier version
of this file pinned 30 models by API id; the only thing that achieved was failing
the weekly job -- and blocking 22 correct prices -- the week Mistral renamed six
KEYS ARE CARD NAMES, exactly as the page states them: 'devstral 2', not
'devstral-medium-latest'. This is a deliberate change from an earlier version. The
page does not say which API id a card refers to, and nothing else on it does
either, so an API id here could only ever be a human's translation, re-checked by
hand forever. A consumer that needs to call the model resolves the id itself, from
_comment_rows: A label is matched exactly first; failing that, the longest entry below that the
label STARTS with wins. The prefix rule exists for two rows only -- training cost
and storage cost -- where Mistral appends an explanatory sentence to the label,
one of which quotes a fee that will itself change. The unit is always in the
leading segment, which is what makes a prefix enough: 'Training cost (/M tokens)'
'expect_suffix' is checked byte-for-byte where the unit is NOT in the label. The
OCR rows read '$4' with the unit stated separately as '/ 1000 pages'; if that
suffix ever changes, per_1k_pages stops meaning what it says, so the row is
dropped and reported rather than published.
A label missing from this table is NOT guessed at -- there is no honest way to
name the unit of a figure whose label this repository does not recognise. That one
row is skipped, the run reports it, and every other price still publishes.
Note 'Audio Input (per min / per M tok)' and 'Text Input (per min / per M tok)':
the card carries the same parenthetical on both rows and says which unit applies
to neither. Reading the audio row as per-minute and the text row as per-M-token is
an INTERPRETATION, written down here rather than inferred in code so a human can
check it. That card is also billed in both units at once; any consumer assuming
one unit per entry silently truncates it.
_comment_products: Cards listed under 'products' are billed beside the models but are not models --
they are priced per call, per image or per month, and there is nothing to call.
The list is an ANNOTATION and gates nothing: a card missing from it is published
as an ordinary model, and a name here that no longer matches any card does
nothing at all. It can never block a price.
The 'Document AI' row carries the marker itself rather than being listed by card,
because it shares the 'ocr 4.1' card with the OCR model: the two collide on
per_1k_pages and are therefore split into an entry each, and only one of them is a
_comment_currency: priceUsd is read and USD is published. The page also states priceEur, and the two
are genuinely different prices rather than a conversion of one another -- 1.25 EUR
against 1.50 USD. No conversion is performed anywhere in this repository.
